title: The Mouse Deer and the Tiger
summary: A hungry tiger wants to eat the mouse deer. With wit and calm, the mouse deer finds a way to escape the tiger's claws. How?
moral: Calm and a clever mind can help us when danger comes. But use your wits for good, and never be arrogant about strength.
pages: That morning the forest was very cool. The little mouse deer drank at the riverbank, singing cheerfully. Suddenly the bushes shook hard, and a big tiger appeared with hungry eyes. 'Hey mouse deer, what luck. I am very hungry!' it roared.
The mouse deer was startled and stepped back. Its heart pounded, but it tried to stay calm. 'Wait, Mr Tiger!' it said. 'I may be small, but I have important news for you.' The tiger stopped, curious.

'Across the river there is another tiger,' whispered the mouse deer. 'He calls himself the King of the Forest and laughs at you!' Hearing that, the tiger was furious. 'How dare he! Show me where he is!'

They reached the riverbank. 'There he is, sir,' said the mouse deer, pointing into the water. The tiger looked and saw a big tiger on the surface of the water. It did not know it was only its own reflection! 'Hey, you! Dare you challenge me?' it roared.
'Grrr!' roared the tiger. Strangely, the tiger in the water also opened its mouth as if roaring back. The tiger grew angrier. 'He dares to roar back at me! Just you wait, I will teach you a lesson!'

The tiger could not wait any longer. It leapt into the river to pounce on its challenger. Splash! The water sprayed high. But there was no tiger! There was only the rippling water around its own body.
While the tiger was confused in the water, the mouse deer slipped behind the bushes. Soaked and cold, the tiger regretted it. 'So I was tricked by my own reflection,' it murmured in shame.
The mouse deer went home with a light heart. It learned that calm and wit can help when danger comes. But that wit must be used for good, not to hurt. And arrogance only harms oneself. The end.
